listing.name: Captain Claw / OpenClaw
listing.summary: Build OpenClaw with upstream instructions and use the CLAW.REZ archive from your own Captain Claw installation.

restrictions.explanation: The released Windows ZIP and PortMaster package include original Captain Claw resources. The upstream source build is the route for using your own original.

steps.title: Build an upstream player
steps.instruction: Use the tagged upstream build instructions to make your player. The Linux build needs the SDL2 libraries and TinyXML listed by upstream. On CMake 4, add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 at configure time for this tag. On Windows the tag provides an upstream Visual Studio solution. Launch the actual OpenClaw player from its working folder, which is Build_Release for the Linux build. The optional Mono launcher edits the configuration.

steps.title: Use your own Captain Claw data
steps.instruction: Keep your original installation intact. Put a separate copy of its CLAW.REZ alongside the source-built player, the project ASSETS.ZIP and the tagged working-folder config.xml. Leave AssetsFolder empty when the files are together. Start the player with that folder as its working folder. Keep the original edition and asset package together.

steps.title: Keep the data from your working copy
steps.instruction: Close the player before copying config.xml and the save file selected by SavesFile, normally SAVES.XML. Keep any edited assets and settings with the working copy. A local config.xml selects that folder. Without it, the Linux player looks under ~/.config/openclaw. Use upstream tools when changing the player.

warnings: The PortMaster launcher can replace CLAW.REZ with its bundled archive. Keep any original you supply outside that working folder.

references.title: Check Mac and Android build availability
references.instruction: Upstream has Mac and Android build material. The reviewed release has neither an Intel or Apple Silicon Mac app nor an Android APK.
